blurb: Small, flat-faced Parisian companion with upright bat ears and a muscular build
description: The French Bulldog is a small companion breed from France with bat ears, a flat face and a short, fine coat, kept mainly as a family pet.
answer: The French Bulldog is a small French companion breed that appeared in Paris in the mid-nineteenth century, apparently from Toy Bulldogs imported from England crossed with local ratters. It is muscular and compact, with a square head, bat-like ears and a flat face, and is now among the most frequently registered breeds in several countries.

body: Lace workers from Nottingham who settled in Normandy brought Toy Bulldogs with them, and a trade in small Bulldogs from England to France followed. The type became known as the Bouledogue Français, and terrier stock is thought to have been added to fix traits such as the long straight ears. American owners set up a breed club and standard favouring the erect bat ear, and the Kennel Club in Britain recognised it separately from the Bulldog in 1905. The AKC ranked it the most popular breed in 2023 and 2024.

The American Kennel Club standard calls for a muscular dog with soft, loose skin forming wrinkles, a large square head, bat ears and dark eyes, with a maximum weight of 28 lb (13 kg). The coat is short, fine and silky. Accepted colors are shades of brindle, fawn, and cream or white with brindle patches (pied).
The breed was developed as a companion and is commonly kept as a household pet. Sources give little detail on temperament, so breed club descriptions are the best guide to individual dogs.

Sources give little detail on exercise needs. Because the flat face makes it hard for the dog to cool itself by panting, the breed is prone to overheating, and several airlines will not carry French Bulldogs.

The breed is susceptible to problems linked to its flat face and skin folds. Conditions reported in the breed include brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome, stenotic nares, ear infections, skin fold dermatitis, skin allergies, hemivertebrae, patellar luxation, intervertebral disc herniation and hereditary cataracts. Over 80% of litters are delivered by Caesarean section, and one 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 9.8 years.

faq.q: How big does a French Bulldog get?
faq.a: French Bulldogs typically stand about 23–36 cm and weigh about 7.5–15 kg; the AKC standard sets a maximum of 13 kg.

faq.q: How long do French Bulldogs live?
faq.a: Figures vary by source: a commonly cited figure is about 11 years, while a 2024 UK study found 9.8 years and a Japanese study 10.2 years.

faq.q: Why do French Bulldogs have breathing problems?
faq.a: Their shortened snout, known as brachycephaly, deforms the upper airway and can obstruct breathing and make it hard to cool down.

faq.q: Is the French Bulldog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the French Bulldog as breed number 101 in Group 9, companion and toy dogs.
